---
title: "Visual Math Lab"
subtitle: "Interactive, browser-based visualizations of numerical methods."
listing:
  - id: latest-listing
    contents: "/apps/*/index.qmd"
    type: grid
    sort: "date desc"
    fields: [image, title, description]
    image-height: "160px"
  # Every app as JSON, for the Random app script below (random-apps.ejs).
  - id: random-apps
    contents: "/apps/*/index.qmd"
    template: random-apps.ejs
---

<style>
/* The hero below carries its own title, so the default Quarto title
   block (rendered separately above it) would just duplicate "Visual
   Math Lab" -- hide it here. Scoped to this page only: the id is
   page-local to the compiled index.html. */
#title-block-header { display: none; }

/* Hero: title, kicker, intro and call-to-action in a left-aligned
   column, with the looping SVG illustration beside it on the right.
   Below 768px the two stack, the illustration under the text.
   Homepage-only, so it lives here. */
.vm-hero {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) minmax(0, 1fr);
  gap: 2rem;
  align-items: center;
  margin: 1rem 0 2.5rem;
}

.vm-hero-text {
  text-align: left;
}

.vm-hero-title {
  margin: 0;
  font-size: clamp(1.75rem, 4vw, 2.75rem);
  font-weight: 700;
  letter-spacing: -0.01em;
}

.vm-hero-kicker {
  margin: 0.5rem 0 0;
  color: var(--vm-text-soft);
  font-size: 1.1rem;
}

.vm-hero-intro {
  margin: 1rem 0 1.25rem;
}

.hero-visual {
  pointer-events: none;
}

.hero-visual-plot {
  display: block;
  width: 100%;
  height: auto;
  aspect-ratio: 460 / 260;
}

@media (max-width: 767.98px) {
  .vm-hero {
    grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr);
    gap: 1rem;
  }
}

.vm-hero-cta {
  display: inline-block;
  padding: 0.55rem 1.35rem;
  border-radius: var(--vm-radius-sm);
  background: var(--vm-accent);
  color: var(--vm-bg);
  font-weight: 500;
  text-decoration: none;
  transition: background-color 80ms cubic-bezier(0.33, 1, 0.68, 1);
}

.vm-hero-cta:hover {
  background: var(--vm-accent-hover);
  color: var(--vm-bg);
  text-decoration: none;
}

.vm-hero-ctas {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: 0.75rem;
}

.vm-hero-cta-secondary {
  background: transparent;
  color: var(--vm-accent);
  box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--vm-accent);
}

.vm-hero-cta-secondary:hover {
  background: var(--vm-surface-hover);
  color: var(--vm-accent);
}

/* "Random app": one app in an <iframe>, framed the way embed.qmd
   tells another site to frame it. In embed mode the chart takes whatever
   height the controls leave, so the frame's height is the whole app's;
   900px is that page's recommendation, and gives every app on the site,
   as of this writing, at least a ~420px chart with no inner scrolling.
   The script below grows this past 900px, never shrinks it, if a future
   app's controls panel would otherwise squeeze the chart smaller than
   that -- see its comment for why that has to be measured rather than
   just read off scrollHeight. */
.vm-featured {
  margin: 1.25rem 0 0;
}

.vm-featured-frame {
  display: block;
  width: 100%;
  height: 900px;
  border: 1px solid var(--vm-border);
  border-radius: var(--vm-radius);
  background: var(--vm-surface);
}

/* Browse-by-topic tiles. */
.vm-topic-grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(15rem, 1fr));
  gap: 1rem;
  margin: 1rem 0 2.5rem;
}

.vm-topic-tile {
  display: block;
  padding: 1rem 1.15rem;
  border: 1px solid var(--vm-border);
  border-radius: var(--vm-radius);
  color: var(--vm-text);
  text-decoration: none !important;
  line-height: 1.45;
  transition: background-color 0.1s ease, border-color 0.1s ease;
}

.vm-topic-tile:hover {
  background: var(--vm-surface-hover);
  border-color: var(--vm-accent);
}

.vm-topic-tile strong {
  display: block;
  margin-bottom: 0.3rem;
  color: var(--vm-accent);
  font-weight: 600;
}

/* Rotation between the hero's six illustration scenes. Every scene's
   internal animations run on one --hero-cycle, and the rotation shows each
   scene for exactly one cycle, starting at a whole multiple of it (the
   --slot delay), so a scene's internal loop is always back at its own
   phase 0 the instant the rotation reveals it. Change the pace here. */
.hero-visual {
  --hero-cycle: 8s;
}

.hero-scene {
  opacity: 0;
  animation-name: hero-scene;
  animation-duration: calc(6 * var(--hero-cycle));
  animation-delay: calc(var(--slot) * var(--hero-cycle));
  animation-timing-function: linear;
  animation-iteration-count: infinite;
}

.hero-scene-newton { --slot: 0; }
.hero-scene-spiro { --slot: 1; }
.hero-scene-kalman { --slot: 2; }
.hero-scene-integral { --slot: 3; }
.hero-scene-sperner { --slot: 4; }
.hero-scene-fixed { --slot: 5; }

@keyframes hero-scene {
  0%, 16.4% { opacity: 1; }
  16.67%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
}

/* Newton's-method loop: exactly one stage is visible at a time (point0,
   then each tangent+point group), crossfading into the next on a shared
   --hero-cycle so they stay in phase forever without any JS driving them.
   Within each group, the tangent/guide lines "draw" in via a moving
   stroke-dashoffset and the new point pops in with a small scale
   overshoot, layered on top of the parent group's opacity crossfade.
   A plain opacity crossfade is low-risk motion, so it's left running
   even under prefers-reduced-motion. */
.hero-newton-point0,
.hero-newton-group1,
.hero-newton-group2,
.hero-newton-group3 {
  opacity: 0;
  animation-duration: var(--hero-cycle);
  animation-timing-function: ease-in-out;
  animation-iteration-count: infinite;
}

.hero-newton-point0 { animation-name: hero-newton-point0; transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: center; }
.hero-newton-group1 { animation-name: hero-newton-group1; }
.hero-newton-group2 { animation-name: hero-newton-group2; }
.hero-newton-group3 { animation-name: hero-newton-group3; }

.hero-newton-draw1, .hero-newton-draw2, .hero-newton-draw3 {
  animation-duration: var(--hero-cycle);
  animation-timing-function: ease-out;
  animation-iteration-count: infinite;
}

.hero-newton-pop1, .hero-newton-pop2, .hero-newton-pop3 {
  transform-box: fill-box;
  transform-origin: center;
  animation-duration: var(--hero-cycle);
  animation-timing-function: cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1);
  animation-iteration-count: infinite;
}

.hero-newton-draw1 { animation-name: hero-newton-draw1; }
.hero-newton-draw2 { animation-name: hero-newton-draw2; }
.hero-newton-draw3 { animation-name: hero-newton-draw3; }
.hero-newton-pop1 { animation-name: hero-newton-pop1; }
.hero-newton-pop2 { animation-name: hero-newton-pop2; }
.hero-newton-pop3 { animation-name: hero-newton-pop3; }

@keyframes hero-newton-point0 {
  0%, 100% { opacity: 0; transform: scale(0.3); }
  5% { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1.15); }
  8%, 17% { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1); }
  23% { opacity: 0; transform: scale(1); }
}

@keyframes hero-newton-group1 {
  0%, 17%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
  23%, 35% { opacity: 1; }
  41% { opacity: 0; }
}

@keyframes hero-newton-group2 {
  0%, 35%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
  41%, 53% { opacity: 1; }
  59% { opacity: 0; }
}

@keyframes hero-newton-group3 {
  0%, 53%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
  59%, 83% { opacity: 1; }
  90% { opacity: 0; }
}

@keyframes hero-newton-draw1 {
  0%, 23% { stroke-dashoffset: 160; }
  29%, 100% { stroke-dashoffset: 0; }
}

@keyframes hero-newton-draw2 {
  0%, 41% { stroke-dashoffset: 160; }
  47%, 100% { stroke-dashoffset: 0; }
}

@keyframes hero-newton-draw3 {
  0%, 59% { stroke-dashoffset: 160; }
  65%, 100% { stroke-dashoffset: 0; }
}

@keyframes hero-newton-pop1 {
  0%, 27% { transform: scale(0.3); }
  32% { transform: scale(1.18); }
  35%, 100% { transform: scale(1); }
}

@keyframes hero-newton-pop2 {
  0%, 45% { transform: scale(0.3); }
  50% { transform: scale(1.18); }
  53%, 100% { transform: scale(1); }
}

@keyframes hero-newton-pop3 {
  0%, 63% { transform: scale(0.3); }
  69% { transform: scale(1.25); }
  73%, 100% { transform: scale(1); }
}

/* Noisy-to-smooth filter loop: the scattered measurements fade in first,
   then the filtered estimate draws itself across left to right via a
   moving stroke-dashoffset, holds, then everything fades out together.
   Same --hero-cycle as the Newton scene, for the same reason. */
.hero-kalman-dots, .hero-kalman-smooth {
  opacity: 0;
  animation-duration: var(--hero-cycle);
  animation-timing-function: ease-in-out;
  animation-iteration-count: infinite;
}

.hero-kalman-dots { animation-name: hero-kalman-dots; }
.hero-kalman-smooth { animation-name: hero-kalman-smooth; }

@keyframes hero-kalman-dots {
  0%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
  8%, 83% { opacity: 1; }
  92% { opacity: 0; }
}

@keyframes hero-kalman-smooth {
  0%, 100% { opacity: 0; stroke-dashoffset: 680; }
  8% { opacity: 1; stroke-dashoffset: 680; }
  13% { stroke-dashoffset: 680; }
  55% { stroke-dashoffset: 0; }
  83% { opacity: 1; stroke-dashoffset: 0; }
  92% { opacity: 0; stroke-dashoffset: 0; }
}

/* Sperner's-lemma loop: the triangle assembles itself piece by piece
   (outer edges, corner colors, inner subdivision, midpoint colors, then
   the trichromatic triangle highlight), holds the complete picture, then
   fades out together. Same --hero-cycle as the other scenes. */
.hero-sperner-outer, .hero-sperner-corners, .hero-sperner-inner, .hero-sperner-mid-dots, .hero-sperner-highlight {
  opacity: 0;
  animation-duration: var(--hero-cycle);
  animation-timing-function: ease-in-out;
  animation-iteration-count: infinite;
}

.hero-sperner-draw-outer, .hero-sperner-draw-inner {
  animation-duration: var(--hero-cycle);
  animation-timing-function: ease-out;
  animation-iteration-count: infinite;
}

.hero-sperner-pop-outer, .hero-sperner-pop-inner {
  transform-box: fill-box;
  transform-origin: center;
  animation-duration: var(--hero-cycle);
  animation-timing-function: cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1);
  animation-iteration-count: infinite;
}

.hero-sperner-highlight { transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: center; }

.hero-sperner-outer { animation-name: hero-sperner-outer; }
.hero-sperner-corners { animation-name: hero-sperner-corners; }
.hero-sperner-inner { animation-name: hero-sperner-inner; }
.hero-sperner-mid-dots { animation-name: hero-sperner-mid-dots; }
.hero-sperner-highlight { animation-name: hero-sperner-highlight, hero-sperner-highlight-pop; }
.hero-sperner-draw-outer { animation-name: hero-sperner-draw-outer; }
.hero-sperner-draw-inner { animation-name: hero-sperner-draw-inner; }
.hero-sperner-pop-outer { animation-name: hero-sperner-pop-outer; }
.hero-sperner-pop-inner { animation-name: hero-sperner-pop-inner; }

@keyframes hero-sperner-outer {
  0%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
  1%, 83% { opacity: 1; }
  90% { opacity: 0; }
}

@keyframes hero-sperner-draw-outer {
  0%, 1% { stroke-dashoffset: 220; }
  15%, 100% { stroke-dashoffset: 0; }
}

@keyframes hero-sperner-corners {
  0%, 10%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
  13%, 83% { opacity: 1; }
  90% { opacity: 0; }
}

@keyframes hero-sperner-pop-outer {
  0%, 10% { transform: scale(0.3); }
  15% { transform: scale(1.2); }
  18%, 100% { transform: scale(1); }
}

@keyframes hero-sperner-inner {
  0%, 15%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
  17%, 83% { opacity: 1; }
  90% { opacity: 0; }
}

@keyframes hero-sperner-draw-inner {
  0%, 17% { stroke-dashoffset: 110; }
  30%, 100% { stroke-dashoffset: 0; }
}

@keyframes hero-sperner-mid-dots {
  0%, 28%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
  31%, 83% { opacity: 1; }
  90% { opacity: 0; }
}

@keyframes hero-sperner-pop-inner {
  0%, 28% { transform: scale(0.3); }
  34% { transform: scale(1.2); }
  37%, 100% { transform: scale(1); }
}

@keyframes hero-sperner-highlight {
  0%, 33%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
  40%, 83% { opacity: 1; }
  90% { opacity: 0; }
}

@keyframes hero-sperner-highlight-pop {
  0%, 33% { transform: scale(0.5); }
  40% { transform: scale(1.15); }
  44%, 100% { transform: scale(1); }
}
/* Spirograph loop: the outer hypotrochoid draws itself (a moving
   stroke-dashoffset over a pathLength of 1), the inner epitrochoid
   follows, both hold, then fade out together. */
.hero-spiro-a, .hero-spiro-b {
  stroke-dasharray: 1;
  stroke-dashoffset: 1;
  animation-duration: var(--hero-cycle);
  animation-timing-function: ease-in-out;
  animation-iteration-count: infinite;
}

.hero-spiro-a { animation-name: hero-spiro-a; }
.hero-spiro-b { animation-name: hero-spiro-b; }

@keyframes hero-spiro-a {
  0% { stroke-dashoffset: 1; opacity: 1; }
  55% { stroke-dashoffset: 0; }
  86% { opacity: 1; }
  94%, 100% { stroke-dashoffset: 0; opacity: 0; }
}

@keyframes hero-spiro-b {
  0%, 35% { stroke-dashoffset: 1; opacity: 1; }
  75% { stroke-dashoffset: 0; }
  86% { opacity: 1; }
  94%, 100% { stroke-dashoffset: 0; opacity: 0; }
}

/* Numerical-integration loop: midpoint-rule rectangles grow up from the
   axis, 4 of them, then 8, then 16, each refinement replacing the last,
   until the exact area fills in under the curve; then everything fades. */
.hero-integral-rects, .hero-integral-area {
  opacity: 0;
  transform-box: fill-box;
  transform-origin: bottom;
  animation-duration: var(--hero-cycle);
  animation-timing-function: ease-out;
  animation-iteration-count: infinite;
}

.hero-integral-n4 { animation-name: hero-integral-n4; }
.hero-integral-n8 { animation-name: hero-integral-n8; }
.hero-integral-n16 { animation-name: hero-integral-n16; }
.hero-integral-area { animation-name: hero-integral-area; }

@keyframes hero-integral-n4 {
  0%, 4% { opacity: 1; transform: scaleY(0); }
  14% { transform: scaleY(1); }
  28% { opacity: 1; transform: scaleY(1); }
  32%, 100% { opacity: 0; transform: scaleY(1); }
}

@keyframes hero-integral-n8 {
  0%, 28% { opacity: 0; transform: scaleY(0); }
  30% { opacity: 1; }
  40% { transform: scaleY(1); }
  52% { opacity: 1; transform: scaleY(1); }
  56%, 100% { opacity: 0; transform: scaleY(1); }
}

@keyframes hero-integral-n16 {
  0%, 52% { opacity: 0; transform: scaleY(0); }
  54% { opacity: 1; }
  64% { transform: scaleY(1); }
  86% { opacity: 1; transform: scaleY(1); }
  94%, 100% { opacity: 0; transform: scaleY(1); }
}

@keyframes hero-integral-area {
  0%, 66% { opacity: 0; }
  74%, 86% { opacity: 1; }
  94%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
}

/* Fixed-point-iteration loop: from a starting guess on the axis, the
   cobweb (up to the curve, across to y = x, repeat) draws itself in and
   spirals onto the fixed point of cos x, which pops in once it lands. */
.hero-fixed-web, .hero-fixed-start, .hero-fixed-point {
  transform-box: fill-box;
  transform-origin: center;
  animation-duration: var(--hero-cycle);
  animation-iteration-count: infinite;
}

.hero-fixed-web {
  stroke-dasharray: 1;
  animation-name: hero-fixed-web;
  animation-timing-function: ease-out;
}

.hero-fixed-start { animation-name: hero-fixed-start; animation-timing-function: ease-in-out; }

.hero-fixed-point {
  opacity: 0;
  animation-name: hero-fixed-point;
  animation-timing-function: cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1);
}

@keyframes hero-fixed-web {
  0%, 8% { stroke-dashoffset: 1; opacity: 1; }
  68% { stroke-dashoffset: 0; }
  86% { opacity: 1; }
  94%, 100% { stroke-dashoffset: 0; opacity: 0; }
}

@keyframes hero-fixed-start {
  0% { opacity: 0; transform: scale(0.3); }
  6% { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1); }
  86% { opacity: 1; }
  94%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
}

@keyframes hero-fixed-point {
  0%, 66% { opacity: 0; transform: scale(0.3); }
  72% { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1.25); }
  76%, 86% { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1); }
  94%, 100% { opacity: 0; transform: scale(1); }
}
</style>

::: {.vm-hero}
<div class="vm-hero-text">
<h1 class="vm-hero-title">Visual Math Lab</h1>
<p class="vm-hero-kicker">A picture is worth a thousand equations.</p>
<p class="vm-hero-intro">Here you'll find root finders, ODE solvers, splines, filters and the odd spirograph, all running live in your browser. Change the inputs and watch what the method does. Apps come loaded with examples, including ones where things go wrong, because seeing a method fail teaches as much as seeing it work.</p>
<div class="vm-hero-ctas">
<a class="vm-hero-cta" href="#browse-topics">Browse by topic</a>
<a class="vm-hero-cta vm-hero-cta-secondary" href="#gallery">Browse the gallery</a>
</div>
</div>
<div class="hero-visual">
<!-- Decorative backdrop: a looping rotation of Newton's method, a spirograph, a filter smoothing a noisy signal, the midpoint rule, Sperner's lemma and fixed-point iteration. -->
<svg class="hero-visual-plot" viewBox="0 0 460 260" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true">
  <defs>
    <filter id="hero-newton-glow" x="-60%" y="-60%" width="220%" height="220%">
      <feGaussianBlur stdDeviation="2.5" result="blur" />
      <feMerge>
        <feMergeNode in="blur" />
        <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic" />

    </filter>
    <linearGradient id="hero-sperner-rainbow" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="100%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#ca8a04" />
      <stop offset="50%" stop-color="#0d9488" />
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#c026d3" />
    </linearGradient>
  </defs>
  <!-- scene 1/6: Newton's method finding a root of f(x) = x^2 - 2, starting from x = 2.2 -->
  <g class="hero-scene hero-scene-newton">
    <line x1="20" y1="172.8" x2="440" y2="172.8" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" />
    <polyline fill="none" stroke="#94a3b8" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"
      points="20.0,226.3 26.0,227.5 32.0,228.7 38.0,229.8 44.0,230.7 50.0,231.5 56.0,232.2 62.0,232.8 68.0,233.2 74.0,233.6 80.0,233.8 86.0,233.9 92.0,233.9 98.0,233.7 104.0,233.4 110.0,233.1 116.0,232.6 122.0,231.9 128.0,231.2 134.0,230.3 140.0,229.3 146.0,228.2 152.0,227.0 158.0,225.7 164.0,224.2 170.0,222.6 176.0,220.9 182.0,219.1 188.0,217.2 194.0,215.1 200.0,212.9 206.0,210.6 212.0,208.2 218.0,205.6 224.0,203.0 230.0,200.2 236.0,197.3 242.0,194.3 248.0,191.1 254.0,187.9 260.0,184.5 266.0,181.0 272.0,177.4 278.0,173.6 284.0,169.8 290.0,165.8 296.0,161.7 302.0,157.5 308.0,153.1 314.0,148.7 320.0,144.1 326.0,139.4 332.0,134.6 338.0,129.6 344.0,124.6 350.0,119.4 356.0,114.1 362.0,108.7 368.0,103.1 374.0,97.5 380.0,91.7 386.0,85.8 392.0,79.8 398.0,73.7 404.0,67.4 410.0,61.0 416.0,54.5 422.0,47.9 428.0,41.2 434.0,34.3 440.0,27.3" />
    <circle class="hero-newton-point0" cx="385.8" cy="86.0" r="7" fill="#dc2626" stroke="white" stroke-width="1.5" />
    <g class="hero-newton-group1">

      <line x1="298.4" y1="172.8" x2="298.4" y2="160.0" stroke="#94a3b8" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-dasharray="3,4" />
      <circle class="hero-newton-pop1" cx="298.4" cy="160.0" r="7" fill="#dc2626" stroke="white" stroke-width="1.5" />

    <g class="hero-newton-group2">
      <line class="hero-newton-draw2" x1="298.4" y1="160.0" x2="280.2" y2="172.8" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-dasharray="160" filter="url(#hero-newton-glow)" />
      <line x1="280.2" y1="172.8" x2="280.2" y2="172.2" stroke="#94a3b8" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-dasharray="3,4" />

    <g class="hero-newton-group3">
      <line class="hero-newton-draw3" x1="280.2" y1="172.2" x2="279.3" y2="172.8" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-dasharray="160" filter="url(#hero-newton-glow)" />
      <circle class="hero-newton-pop3" cx="279.3" cy="172.8" r="7" fill="#16a34a" stroke="white" stroke-width="1.5" filter="url(#hero-newton-glow)" />
    </g>
  </g>
  <!-- scene 2/6: two spirographs tracing themselves out -->

## Random app

<p id="vm-featured-description"></p>

<div class="vm-featured">
<iframe id="vm-featured-frame" class="vm-featured-frame" title="A Visual Math Lab app" loading="lazy"></iframe>
</div>

::: {#random-apps}
:::

<script>
// Picks the app the frame below shows and writes its description above it.
// The apps come from the random-apps listing just above (random-apps.ejs),
// which Quarto fills with every apps/*/index.qmd at render time -- not from
// the Gallery listing further down, which List.js paginates after load, so
// its DOM doesn't hold the full set.
(function () {
  var data = document.getElementById("vm-random-apps")
  var frame = document.getElementById("vm-featured-frame")
  var description = document.getElementById("vm-featured-description")
  if (!data || !frame || !description) return
  var apps = JSON.parse(data.textContent)
  if (apps.length === 0) return

  var app = apps[Math.floor(Math.random() * apps.length)]
  var href = "apps/" + app.slug + "/index.html"
  frame.src = href + "?embed=1"
  frame.title = app.title

  var link = document.createElement("a")
  link.href = href
  link.textContent = app.title
  description.append(link, ": " + app.description)

  // Keeps the frame on this page's theme. The frame is its own document,
  // and Quarto reads the saved theme only when a page loads, so a toggle
  // here left the app in the old theme until a reload. Same-origin, so
  // flip the frame's own toggle whenever the two disagree. The comparison
  // is what makes the observer safe on <body>, whose class list also
  // changes when the sidebar opens.
  //
  // Quarto's toggle flips the theme saved in localStorage, not the page it
  // runs on, and this page's toggle has already saved the new one -- so the
  // frame's toggle alone would flip it straight back. Saving the frame's
  // own (the other value) first makes its toggle save this page's again.
  var SCHEME_KEY = "quarto-color-scheme"
  var isDark = function (doc) {
    return doc.body.classList.contains("quarto-dark")
  }
  var syncTheme = function () {
    try {
      var inner = frame.contentWindow
      if (!inner || !inner.document.body || !inner.quartoToggleColorScheme) return
      if (isDark(inner.document) === isDark(document)) return
      var saved = localStorage.getItem(SCHEME_KEY)
      if (saved === "alternate") {
        localStorage.setItem(SCHEME_KEY, "default")
      } else {
        localStorage.setItem(SCHEME_KEY, "alternate")
      }
      inner.quartoToggleColorScheme()
    } catch (e) {
      // Cross-origin: leave the frame on the theme it loaded with.
    }
  }
  new MutationObserver(syncTheme).observe(document.body, {attributes: true, attributeFilter: ["class"]})
  frame.addEventListener("load", syncTheme)

  // Grows the frame past its 900px default if this app's controls panel
  // would otherwise leave the chart shorter than FIT_CHART_HEIGHT. Can't
  // just read the embedded page's scrollHeight and copy it over -- the
  // chart is a flex-grow item (see mathviz's chrome/embed.css) that
  // always expands to fill whatever height the frame gives it, so it has
  // no natural height of its own to measure; scrollHeight would just echo
  // the frame's current height back. What does have a natural height is
  // everything *else* in the app -- the panel, any always-live slider bar
  // -- since those aren't flex-grow items. Sum those and add the chart
  // height we actually want, and that total is what the frame needs to be
  // for the chart to get that much room without inner scrolling.
  //
  // Same-origin (this page only ever embeds this site's own pages), so
  // contentDocument is readable directly; wrapped in try/catch as a
  // fail-soft in case that ever stops being true. A ResizeObserver rather
  // than a one-shot measurement on "load", because OJS/Plotly finish
  // rendering well after that event fires -- the observer re-measures as
  // the panel settles into its final size. Grows only, never shrinks below
  // the CSS default, so a short app doesn't visibly collapse the frame it
  // started in.
  var FIT_CHART_HEIGHT = 420
  frame.addEventListener("load", function () {
    try {
      var doc = frame.contentDocument
      var appRoot = doc.querySelector(".vm-app-active")
      var chartBlock = appRoot ? appRoot.querySelector(".ojs-chart-block") : null
      if (!appRoot || !chartBlock) return
      // Only a Plotly chart is the flex-grow, no-natural-height case: the
      // :has(.js-plotly-plot) rule in mathviz's chrome/embed.css is
      // what gives .ojs-chart-block flex-grow: 1, so reading it back here
      // (rather than re-deriving ".js-plotly-plot exists") is what keeps
      // this in step with that CSS. A page whose chart is Observable
      // Plot/inline SVG (.ojs-svg-block, e.g. the Sperner pages) never
      // matches it, so its chart-block sizes to its own content like any
      // other sibling -- no padding added on top. distribution-relationships
      // is the case that first caught this: its actual visual is a plain
      // .cell outside .ojs-chart-block entirely, and its .ojs-chart-block
      // (a *secondary* chart, empty until a node is clicked) has no Plotly
      // in it either -- padding it by FIT_CHART_HEIGHT regardless nearly
      // doubled the frame for no reason.
      var fit = function () {
        var isFlexFilled = frame.contentWindow.getComputedStyle(chartBlock).flexGrow !== "0"
        var siblingsHeight = 0
        for (var i = 0; i < appRoot.children.length; i++) {
          var child = appRoot.children[i]
          if (child === chartBlock && isFlexFilled) continue
          var style = frame.contentWindow.getComputedStyle(child)
          if (style.display === "none") continue
          var rect = child.getBoundingClientRect()
          siblingsHeight += rect.height + parseFloat(style.marginTop) + parseFloat(style.marginBottom)
        }
        var required = Math.ceil(siblingsHeight + (isFlexFilled ? FIT_CHART_HEIGHT : 0))
        if (required > frame.getBoundingClientRect().height) {
          frame.style.height = required + "px"
        }
      }
      // chartBlock is observed too, not just skipped in the sum above --
      // .js-plotly-plot mounts asynchronously well after "load", and until
      // it does, flexGrow reads "0" and chartBlock is sized like a normal
      // sibling (harmless: it's empty, so it contributes ~0). Its own
      // resize when Plotly finally mounts is what re-triggers fit() with
      // isFlexFilled now true; nothing else on the page necessarily
      // resizes again on its own.
      var observer = new ResizeObserver(fit)
      for (var i = 0; i < appRoot.children.length; i++) {
        observer.observe(appRoot.children[i])
      }
    } catch (e) {
      // Cross-origin, or the embedded page's markup doesn't match -- keep
      // the 900px CSS default.
    }
  })
})()
</script>

## Built with

[Quarto](https://quarto.org), [Observable JS](https://observablehq.com), [Plotly.js](https://plotly.com/javascript/), [math.js](https://mathjs.org), and [mathviz](https://github.com/apurvanakade/mathviz).
